compared.title: The derived limit of an inverse system of complexes fits into the canonical product distinguished triangle
hypotheses_conclusions_evidence:
\label{lemma-distinguished-triangle-Rlim}
Let $K = (K_n^\bullet)$ be an object of $D(\textit{Ab}(\mathbf{N}))$.
There exists a canonical distinguished triangle
$$
R\lim K \to \prod\nolimits_n K_n^\bullet \to \prod\nolimits_n K_n^\bullet
\to R\lim K[1]
$$
in $D(\textit{Ab})$. In other words, $R\lim K$ is a derived limit
of the inverse system $(K_n^\bullet)$ of $D(\textit{Ab})$, see
Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-derived-limit}.

compared.title: Derived limits of bounded-below inverse systems exist with countable products
hypotheses_conclusions_evidence:
\label{lemma-inverse-limit-bounded-below}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category with countable products and
enough injectives. Let $(K_n)$ be an inverse system of $D^+(\mathcal{A})$.
Then $R\lim K_n$ exists.
